<p>What I love most about this issue is the new API launched by CrUX, which can pull out the data of a single web page. There is also the first episode of the Google Webmaster Podcast, which is 30 minutes long but the content is very light. I recommend listening to it! Other updates are mostly focused on tools or news, and there are not many important updates directly related to SEO.</p>

<h2 id="toc-1">Google plans to pay news media for content</h2>
<p>Google plans to start a program in the second half of this year to pay its partner news media in exchange for high-quality content. This plan will be launched first in Germany, Brazil, and Australia.</p>
<p>The interest relationship between Google and the journalism industry has always been conflicting. Google wants to collect content and provide it to searchers, but the journalism industry does not want the content it produces to be provided for free and can only earn advertising revenue. This project hopes to bring new progress in the integration between Google and news media pages.</p>
<p>link:<a href="https://www.blog.google/outreach-initiatives/google-news-initiative/licensing-program-support-news-industry-/">official announcement</a> / <a href="https://newtalk.tw/news/view/2020-06-29/428029">new head shell report</a></p>
<hr class="wp-block-separator"/>
</div></div>
<div class="wp-block-group"><div class="wp-block-group__inner-container">
<h2 id="toc-2">GSC project integrates with GA to provide more information - Beta testing</h2>
<p>Some webmasters received a test invitation letter, which stated that Google Search Console plans to integrate with Google Analytics to provide webmasters with more useful information.</p>
<p>This test has not yet been officially launched, and only some webmasters have received such a letter. However, a reporter from Search Engine Rountable claimed to have seen the interface and provided text information in<a href="https://www.seroundtable.com/google-search-console-insights-beta-29691.html" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">His report</a>in.</p>

<div class="wp-block-group"><div class="wp-block-group__inner-container">
<h2 id="toc-3">Chrome User Experience Reporting API</h2>
<p>Chrome's user experience report used to be only available through BigQuery. Now the official announcement of this API allows everyone to easily capture the user experience data of the website. The most special thing is,<strong>You can see the information of a single web page</strong>! (In BigQuery, data is integrated on a domain basis).
The information that</p>
<p>can capture is very complete, including<a href="./core-web-vitals-lcp-fid-cls.html" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Core indicators of website experience</a>, 75 percentile....etc. new data points.</p>
<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img alt="chrome user experience reporting API" class="wp-image-1479" decoding="async" height="504" loading="lazy" src="./wp-content/uploads/2020/06/chrome%E7%94%A8%E6%88%B6%E9%AB%94%E9%A9%97%E5%A0%B1%E5%91%8AAPI-1024x504.png" width="1024"/><figcaption>API test page, you can enter "origin" or "url" plus the URL</figcaption></figure>
<p>link:<a href="https://web.dev/chrome-ux-report-api/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">official announcement</a> / <a href="https://developers.google.com/web/tools/chrome-user-experience-report/api/reference/rest/v1/records/queryRecord?apix=true&amp;apix_params=%7B%22resource%22%3A%7B%22origin%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fwww.google.com%22%7D%7D" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">API test page</a></p>
<hr class="wp-block-separator"/>
</div></div>
<div class="wp-block-group"><div class="wp-block-group__inner-container">
<h2 id="toc-4">Chrome - Web page paragraph link creation plug-in</h2>
<p>Chrome’s “Scroll to Text Fragment” function (Scroll to Text Fragment) has been used frequently since it was launched, and it has also been used on digital engines many times before.
Introduction to<a href="https://www.facebook.com/searchenginecommunity/photos/a.193015414769742/683930425678236/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"></a>. This Chrome plug-in allows users to easily select a paragraph of text and make a paragraph link.</p>

<h2 id="toc-5">Use GA to record content that appears in featured snippets</h2>
<p>The last e-newsletter mentioned that Google began to add the Scroll to Text function to the content of the featured snippets, and links began to appear.
Parameters of<code>:~:text=</code>. Some foreign netizens have taken advantage of this feature to use GTM to send the text that appears in the selected excerpts to GA.</p>
<p>This step allows SEO personnel to better understand which text on the web page appears in the featured snippet, which is quite cool.</p>
<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img alt="GA Record Featured Excerpts" class="wp-image-1482" decoding="async" height="599" loading="lazy" src="./wp-content/uploads/2020/06/fragment-data-showing-google-analytics-1024x599.jpg" width="1024"/></figure>
<p>link:<a href="https://brodieclark.com/track-featured-snippet-chrome-google-tag-manager/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Record Selected Excerpt Text Guide</a></p>
<hr class="wp-block-separator"/>
</div></div>
<div class="wp-block-group"><div class="wp-block-group__inner-container">
<h2 id="toc-6">To experience the AMP website, should I use the normal version or the AMP version?</h2>
<p>Many AMP websites will have two versions, a general version and a normal version. Someone asked John Mueller: "Which version of the website experience will Google's algorithm use as a reference?"</p>
<p>John's answer is: "Google uses the version seen by the user as the basis, so if the user sees your AMP page on a mobile phone, then we will use the core metric score of the AMP page to score."</p>

<h2 id="toc-7">Bing Update Webmaster Guide</h2>
<p>Bing recently updated their webmaster guidelines, and in the ranking section, they listed six major items:</p>
<ul><li>Relevance</li><li>Quality and Credibility</li><li>User Engagement</li><li>Freshness</li><li>Location</li><li>Page Load Time</li></ul>

<h2 id="toc-8">Google launches two new news media data dashboards</h2>
<p>Google’s News Initiative has updated two data dashboards for websites in the news media industry, namely “News Consumer Insights” and “Realtime Content Insights”. Just connect your own GA and you can use it.</p>
<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img alt="Illustration for SEO e-Newsletter Issue 11 – 2020.06.16~2020.06.30" class="wp-image-1486" decoding="async" height="462" loading="lazy" src="./wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Google%E5%AA%92%E9%AB%94%E5%84%80%E9%8C%B6%E6%9D%BF-1024x462.png" width="1024"/><figcaption>real-time data monitoring dashboard</figcaption></figure>

<h2 id="toc-9">Official Podcast: Search Off the Road Episode 1</h2>
<p>This is the first episode of the podcast hosted by John, Martin, and Gary. It is quite life-like and contains some interesting information. For example, Gary mentioned the recent nofollow changes. He discussed with other search engines and found that most search engines have already crawled nofollow links!</p>
